transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neil (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Head of ML, Verdant), Carlos Mendes (Engineering Manager, Verdant), Aisha Khan (CTO, Verdant)
Shared artifacts: Verdant discovery deck (link: https://redwood.app/deck/verdant), benchmark spreadsheet (shared drive link)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand Verdant's current retrieval stack, eval criteria for embeddings + rerank, vector DB integration, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private fits their latency/SLA/data residency needs. Next steps agreed: send pricing, run benchmarks, share sample data.

00:00 Maya: ok thanks everyone for jumping on, we'll do a quick intro, I think Priya wanted to kick off with current stack, yeah?
00:14 Priya: yeah thanks Maya, um so quick context Verdant is a B2B search product for scientific publications, we currently run a hybrid search — BM25 + TF-IDF on Elastic and then we do a light neural rerank, but it's slow at scale, like when we have thousands of concurrent requests latency spikes.
00:29 Carlos: also we shard across regions for data residency, so any solution needs to play nice with regional VPCs or at least allow us to keep vectors in eu-west and na-east.
00:44 Maya: got it, regional residency, sharding. quick question on scale — what are you seeing in qps and index size?
00:53 Priya: today index is ~50M documents, embeddings at 1536 dims, we store dense vectors separately in a Pinecone instance right now, around 500M vectors projected in 6 months if we onboard more corpora. QPS average 300 but bursts to 2k.
01:10 Liam: 1536 dims — cool, that aligns with some open models. For throughput, are you doing real-time single-shot queries or batch scoring?
01:19 Priya: mostly real-time, some bulk reindexing nightly. Most queries are top-k (k=10) with metadata filters (journal, year) and then a rerank model for final ordering. Rerank is expensive because we fetch candidates and then run a cross-encoder.
01:34 Carlos: one of our pain points is the latency from vector DB + cross-encoder, plus network hops between services, we'd like to reduce overall P99.
01:44 Maya: makes sense. do you have latency SLOs?
01:47 Aisha: for customer-facing search we target p95 < 200ms and p99 < 600ms. Anything above that causes a noticeable UX hit.
01:57 Maya: ok that's helpful. quick high-level on options: Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict residency). We have a recommended architecture for embeddings + reranking where we can either host the vector index in your cloud with Redwood Dedicated or integrate with your existing vector DB and handle model serving for rerank.
02:18 Priya: what's the tradeoff if we keep Pinecone vs bringing index into Redwood Dedicated?
02:24 Liam: good question — if you keep Pinecone, Redwood can call it as a candidate store; we handle embedding generation and rerank in our runtime. That adds a network hop but minimal if co-located. If you move index into Dedicated, we can colocate embeddings and rerank on the same GPU nodes, leverage KV cache and batching, and reduce end-to-end latency. But Dedicated has commitment and typically better latency/cost for high qps.
02:46 Priya: what about dimensionality? we use 1536; do you recommend reducing dims or quantizing?
02:53 Liam: 1536 is common. For Dedicated we support quantized models and FP16 inference to shrink memory. We also have intelligent model/kernel selection so for nearest neighbor search it's often fine to use product quantization or HNSW variants at 256-512 effective dims with minimal quality loss depending on your recall tolerance. We should run offline evals to measure recall drop.
03:15 Carlos: and hybrid search — we want BM25 + embeddings, do you support that natively?
03:21 Maya: yes we often recommend hybrid rerank: BM25 for recall and embeddings for semantic scoring, then a cross-encoder for final ranking. Redwood's routing can do hybrid pipelines, and we have examples integrating with Elastic/OpenSearch plus a vector store.
03:36 Priya: curious about throughput — with our bursts to 2k qps, do you recommend Dedicated?
03:41 Liam: for sustained high QPS and tight p99, Dedicated or Private gives better predictable throughput. Hosted can handle bursts but you may see throttling or fallback to cheaper model variants. Dedicated lets you size GPU pools, autoscale, and use burst capacity.
03:56 Priya: any numbers you can share? ballpark tokens/throughput for rerank models or cross-encoders?
04:03 Liam: ballpark: a distilled cross-encoder on A100 80GB with optimized kernels can do ~200-400 reranks/sec depending on sequence length; you can shard rerank across GPUs and use batching for throughput. For embeddings-only vector search at 1536 dims, a single node with AVX/HNSW indexing can serve thousands of small queries/sec — exact depends on index configuration (efConstruction/efSearch). We'll include benchmark numbers in the spreadsheet.
04:30 Aisha: is there support for private KMS or HSM? we need keys for embeddings at rest.
04:36 Maya: yes Private and Dedicated both support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; Hosted supports envelope encryption with BYOK options for enterprise tiers. We'll share security docs.
04:49 Priya: how much effort is data migration if we move from Pinecone to Redwood index?
04:54 Liam: migration tooling exists; ETL is straightforward: export vectors + metadata and we can bulk ingest. For 50M docs it's non-trivial but we've run migrations with parallel bulk loaders; timeline depends on network bandwidth and chunking. We can run an initial pilot with a subset to validate latency/recall.
05:12 Carlos: regarding filters and metadata, will those be pushed down to vector index or do we post-filter?
05:17 Liam: we support indexed metadata filtering (e.g., HNSW + payload filter) and also hybrid where you pre-filter by metadata then run the vector search. Which is better depends on cardinality of filters; we can recommend patterns once we see sample queries.
05:33 Priya: curious about model variants; we have internal evals showing embedding quality varies — do you recommend Redwood models or customer-run models?
05:40 Maya: we curate open models and provide verified performance profiles, but you can bring your own model — we support on-prem/private model hosting and pinning versions. For embeddings we can recommend model+quantization pairs per workload.
05:55 Priya: what about cost — token vs vector storage costs? We're worried about storage growth to 500M vectors.
06:03 Maya: storage costs in Dedicated are predictable (reserved capacity) and you pay for compute + storage separately; Hosted is usage-based and may be more expensive at scale. We'll include a TCO calc.
06:15 Carlos: any existing integrations with Milvus or Weaviate if we want to test in parallel?
06:20 Liam: yes we've integrated with Milvus and Weaviate before; we can run parallel benchmarks against Pinecone and Milvus to compare recall/latency.
06:30 (brief crosstalk)
06:45 Maya: ok we should define success criteria — Priya, what would make Verdant move forward?
06:50 Priya: p99 end-to-end < 400ms on our query mix, recall within 2% of current system for top-10, cost per query < X (we'll share exact target). Also must meet EU data residency and SOC2 requirements.
07:05 Maya: good. quick note: we can do a 4-week pilot: week 1 ingest sample, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 tune index and rerank, week 4 evaluate results and finalize recommendation.
07:18 Aisha: timeline wise procurement needs a 60-day review but pilot can start fast.
07:25 Maya: perfect — next steps recap: I'll send pricing/TCO and security pack; Liam will run 1k-query benchmark on sample when Priya shares dataset; schedule follow-up private deployment deep dive with your network team.
07:40 Priya: sounds good, can you also include typical autoscaling policies and how canary rollouts work for model updates?
07:47 Liam: yes we'll include examples — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants on error. Also tracing hooks so you can map tokens to cost.
07:58 Carlos: one more — logging/audit retention lengths, we sometimes need 7 years for compliance.
08:03 Maya: we have configurable retention for audit logs on enterprise plans; we'll include that in the security doc but will confirm upper limits.
08:12 (speaker label glitch) Speaker 1: yeah totally, um -- also if we test Hybrid BM25 + embeddings, what metric do you recommend for offline eval?
08:22 Liam: nDCG@10 and recall@10 are standard; also measure latency and cost per query. We'll run those in the benchmark.
08:31 Priya: ok thanks all, useful call.
08:34 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.

Action recap (auto): Maya to send pricing/security docs; Liam to run bench and share spreadsheets; Verdant to share sample dataset and query distribution.
